gloss: time signal; hourly chime; time announcement

definitions.gloss: time signal; hourly chime; time announcement
definitions.explanation: A signal — typically a series of beeps, a chime, or a recorded voice — that announces the exact time, especially on the hour. Used by radio and TV broadcasts, telephone services, and clock towers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{時計|とけい}→時計：00677_tokei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{時報|じほう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鳴|な}らした→鳴らす：02381_narasu⟧。
examples.english: The clock chimed the time signal.

examples.japanese: ⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時報|じほう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧⟦{時計|とけい}→時計：00677_tokei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{調|ちょう}{整|せい}した→調整する：10442_chouseisuru⟧。
examples.english: I set my watch by the radio time signal.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{正午|しょうご}→正午：03231_shougo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{放送|ほうそう}→放送：02093_housou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{時報|じほう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流|なが}れる→流れる：01969_nagareru⟧。
examples.english: Every day at noon, a time signal plays from the town's loudspeakers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{電話|でんわ}→電話：01471_denwa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧「117」⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{時報|じほう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: In the past, you could hear the time signal by calling 117 on the phone.

notes:
{時報|じほう} literally combines ⟦{時|じ}→時：09869_ji⟧ (time) and {報|ほう} (report, signal). It refers to any signal that announces the exact time — whether a chime, beep, or recorded announcement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時報|じほう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}る→鳴る：01143_naru⟧: a time signal sounds
- {時報|じほう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{流|なが}す→流す：01968_nagasu⟧: to broadcast a time signal
- {時報|じほう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧: to set (a clock) by the time signal
- ⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時報|じほう}: the radio time signal
- ⟦{正午|しょうご}→正午：03231_shougo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時報|じほう}: the noon time signal

CULTURAL NOTE:
- In Japan, the noon {時報|じほう} broadcast through municipal loudspeakers (⟦{防災|ぼうさい}→防災：07907_bousai⟧⟦{無線|むせん}→無線：09226_musen⟧) is a daily ritual in many cities and towns — a melody such as ⟦{夕焼|ゆうや}け→夕焼け：05045_yuuyake⟧{小|こ}{焼|や}け or a chime indicates noon and 5 PM.
- The classic NHK radio {時報|じほう} consists of three short "pi" beeps followed by a longer "pō" tone, marking the exact start of the next hour.
- The phone-based time service at 117, run by NTT, was widely used to set clocks before networked devices became common.
